steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Eugh... What is this—disgusting floor? What's happening?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Is it the Sea Terrors?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Thiago.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...Amaia.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: What's going on? Didn't you say those Church of the Deep cultists wouldn't show up? They've made a complete mess of the place.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Thiago, I came to say goodbye.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: It's about time for me to, and the opportunity is hard to come by now. That's all it is.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I don't understand.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Thiago.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The Inquisitors are here. A whole three of them.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Jordi's in their hands.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Gah—!

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Don't, Thiago. Jordi came back by his own will. And what can you do against three Inquisitors?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Does he know what it means to be found by the Inquisition?!

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: You've told him so many times that I'd be shocked if he didn't.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: But that's how people are. Reason might tell us to take every advantage and avoid the opposite, but people are so complicated, and you can't judge that so easily. I wouldn't call Jordi a fool for his choice.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Now's not the time to argue over morality—!

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: This is his nature we're talking about. Character, not morality, Mayor Thiago.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: There's a certain beauty in human nature. Even time can't deny that.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: What are you getting at?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Do you hate the Inquisition?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The Sea Terrors have blanketed this town, but remember, Thiago, remember.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Remember that rainy night, when the Penal Battalion charged into town, breaking down doors. The unending screams drowned out the pitter-patter of the rain.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: No, stop...

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: And now?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The sea's brand is spreading across town—have you heard any screams? Have you seen anyone being senselessly slaughtered, or hunted down?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: You haven't.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Right now, all that remains in Gran Faro—

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: —is stillness.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I never knew... that the ocean was so vast.
The sea breeze blows past.
Jordi cannot believe what's before his eyes. He had always thought the sea's horizon was the sky's end.
Not until witnessing this boundless expanse of waves for himself does Jordi—the Ægir—have a sudden question.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Why has humanity never desired to explore this?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...How could we ever determine our position out here? It's not as if the moons are signal beacons, or the stars could be read like a map.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um, why can't we read the stars like a map?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Ask a professional astronomer and find out.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Then... if Ægir really is under the water, then how big is it? Bigger than Iberia?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: There's a handful of genuine Ægir over there. How about you ask them?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: They seem like they have their own worries, though. They're all so solemn.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Shark, what are you listening to?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...The wind.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: There's an offering of kin mingled with the sea breeze. It puts me... much at ease.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: She gets more like this the closer we are to the sea.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Even though in Sal Viento, she was so...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Do you know why?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I could guess, but it would only disturb your judgment. We have a battle before us.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Did you ever attempt to return to the sea, after your narrow escape to shore?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Of course. I failed.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: There was no end to them. They surrounded me. I ran out of strength before I could even swim far.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I tried so, so many times.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But you're still alive.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We are all well aware of the changes in our bodies, Skadi. You included.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Shark may have suffered some injury, but none of my Hunters are so fragile.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And she's the same as us.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: 'Specter.' Once a victim of the Church of the Deep. Originium, absent in the ocean, has affected her in a whole host of ways.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Why bring along such an uncertain element?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We are going home. It does not concern you.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Home? But circumstances in Ægir can hardly be better than in Iberia.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Raise your lantern, Inquisitor. Let's prepare to greet our first enemies.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Oh. They've come.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: One final question.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Are there really only three Abyssal Hunters?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: If there were others, I would have long since found them.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...What compels you to ask?

steps.name: Unexpected Sea Terrors
steps.text: (Ominous slithering sounds)

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Is this ship's course true?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Undoubtedly.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...Then the Sea Terrors are becoming more explicitly hostile as we approach the Eye of Iberia.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Perhaps it is already their nest. Fighting them aboard this ship would waste far too much time.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Skadi, Shark, defend this vessel. Keep an eye on the primitive signal navigation facilities while you're at it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I will enter the sea.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'll go with you.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You are stronger in the sea, but so are they. And we cannot bleed down there; the risk is too high.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wh-What's wrong?! Are there monsters attacking again?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: No, I can't see any! We don't know what's happening under the water, but—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: That muffled booming! What's going on down there? Is she fighting below?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: She's just... moving. She's faster in the water.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...How can anyone move faster through water than air?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Habit, I guess. Or maybe it's a skill.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: The Sea Terrors are following her. She's opened up a passage.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Irene, take Breogan's descendant and continue to steer.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Pick up speed before the enemy surrounds us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They've left. The seas won't be peaceful.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: If you worry for them, we'd best hurry and finish up our business.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Gran Faro is only an outpost to recapture the lighthouse. Retaking it is all that matters.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm surprised that Iberia can already exploit Ægir technology to resist the encroaching nethersea brand.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Regardless, the rate of its evolution is faster than any one scientist's genius. If we seek victory, we must use whatever we can.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even an army, I see.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...This is an plain, unremarkable town.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Perhaps there are more strategic locations waiting for the Inquisition to recapture them, one by one. More favorable battlefields, grander walls and fortifications.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But, sometimes, it's fine to start with what's at hand.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: However many Iberians are willing to fight to the death against the waves, that is how many soldiers we can field.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Let us begin the cleanup.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Unabated slithering sounds)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Hey... Are we still not there yet?!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: A-According to the nautical map, we should be able to at least see it by now...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: High Inquisitor! We have to head deeper in, or else—

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: No.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Look up.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What? It's nothing but black overhead, I can't see—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: No... that's not... that's not the sky...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: They've made it their nest by now. Very close to the shore; no wonder their numbers are so great.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: We can just cut them all down. Like before.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...Yes, like before.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Shark?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: So that is... their eye? Why does it feel so familiar?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It has been caked in filth for too long, unable to open its lid.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: I'll clear a path. Jordi, come with us.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ah. O-Okay... I hope I can be of help...

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: No. There's something only you can do.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: If you can't, then we'll have to change strategies and prioritize ensuring that the Inquisition's technicians can make it here safely.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: And in the battle to come, we'll have no time to care for the fate of a solipsistic Ægir.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Got it!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You seem nervous.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Ægir. You don't understand what finally reaching this island again signifies for us.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And what would that be?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Ever since the Penal Battalion discovered remnant signals from the lighthouse, we've made seventeen attempts to make landfall, eight of which succeeded in setting foot on this reef.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Hundreds of soldiers, and three Inquisitors. No one returned alive.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Don't tell me your superior Ægir ethics teach you to respect your heroes, but forsake their memory?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: The High Inquisitor and I... the Iberians will hold a memorial for those who died at sea.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I did not mean to pick at your morals. All I can say is that, in the face of the ocean, we are all alone and weak.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Do as you wish, but we are pressed for time.
A foot falls on the reef.
A colossus hides in the jet-black winds. Only by tilting one's head back and gazing far up can one distinguish it from the murky sky.
The Eye of Iberia.
A final pair of eyes, sealed shut.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: So tall...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: The scale of that statue in town has to be wrong...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: High Inquisitor.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: This is what we once...

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: It is... my first time seeing it as well.
The two remain silent for a moment, dead in their tracks as they look over at this vast spectacle that's survived only in documents and records.
The enduring reality of Iberia goes far beyond what she was taught, Irene thinks. Despite the Abyssal Hunters' ample disdain for them, despite the balance of the nation well and truly crumbling.
Despite it all, this lighthouse is an emblem. Of past glory and wild ambition. Of dreams and the domination of the unknown.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Whatever feelings may roil in your heart at this moment, engrave them all.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: This building, these worn swords and lanterns, these reefs, this ocean.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Carve into your heart just what humanity has built in its struggle. Keep it with you forever, at all times.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: If we do not venerate our sacrifices, our scales are meaningless.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Enter carefully.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Got it!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Have we come home?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No, not yet.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: But if we find what Kal'tsit and the Captain are looking for here, maybe we can.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Just hold on... we're almost there.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It's too quiet.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: But it still stinks.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Yes. The reef is coated in remnant nethersea brand. I can see traces of man-made objects too, rotted for the most part.
Gladiia paces slowly. She looks up at the tower, standing against the tenebrous sky.
The Eye of Iberia is directed towards the heavens, as if upon this finite soil, life cranes its neck, wanting to see the future.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The nations of the land have done all they can to reproduce Breogan's remaining legacy. These so-called lighthouses are an emulation of Ægir technology through and through.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: What can this lighthouse be awaiting, sat in this void and empty sea?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Does it watch the ocean, or the land, I wonder.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Captain.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I know. Within is a Sea Terror nest. The lack of an immediate attack may merely be defensive, a guarding of the den.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It is about time they come.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Ominous slithering sounds)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: There's not... too many.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The sea. The coast is already out of sight.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Sentimental?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No... I just mean, we can't bleed here. It'll be extremely dangerous.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: They can't pierce our skin. So long as you do not cease your dance, these numbers are insufficient to kill us.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (The lighthouse... It really is just like the statue in town.)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (Which means, those blueprints at home really were from my mother and father. For the Eye of Iberia...)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (My parents were once... in this very place.)
Jordi looks back towards the shore.
Each and every day, his mind went back to his view of that overcast shore. A lifeless gray, a hopeless crowd.
But, ah, look at this lighthouse, he thinks.
Uncle Thiago was right. They were all heroes. They were all meant to be legends.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: ...The Abyssal Hunters should be regrouping not far from here. They will be joining this battle too.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Don't forget what you experienced in Sal Viento. Their blood is highly unusual, and Kal'tsit hardly told us everything.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: U-Understood. So they can't be trusted.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: What did you see, beneath the Inquisition?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —Erk.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: 'Seaborn.'

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You should still remember their twistedness, their vitality, their... serenity.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: In Sal Viento, the Hunters did battle such a monster, and emerged victorious.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I... I know that.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You've seen the truth, so now you must reassess your past, and Iberia.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Tear apart the old, swimming through your head! Make your own judgments.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Y-Yes, sir!

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: —(Rough sounds of slithering over reef)—

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: They're ready for us. Withdrawn to defend their nest, waiting for the chance to strike. Here to drive out the invaders.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Jordi. Report?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: R-Right! It's a miracle, really. These control panels outside are still responding, but I'm not sure what theory these things are based on...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I-I'm looking though! I have all those research notes from home with me in my bag!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: ...Be quick about it.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I know! It's this one... No, that's not it... Eek, when did this one get wet?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: High Inquisitor! They're here!
The billows rage forth.
Their arrogance surges dozens of meter high, shattering one day after another, succumbing to the reef and the three moons.
One moon is bright. One moon is dark. These are the moons spoken of throughout time, hung in the sky.
The remaining moon comes from the intervals betwixt the waves, at the peaks of every crest.
The moonlight comes from the title he once believed in.
